Article Title: Vande row: Do they want Kashmiris in jail? J&K CM Omar Abdullah hits back at Congress
Article Text:
Omar Abdullah

SRINAGAR: Does Congress want more Kashmiris to be jailed?” J&K chief minister Omar Abdullah retorted on Thursday, a day after ally Congress criticised him for the rendition of all six stanzas of Vande Mataram at the inaugural ceremony of International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK) on Monday.“It is a statutory obligation. The entire stanza of national song Vande Mataram must be played across the country at the govt events,” the CM said, adding legal action could be taken against those who fail to stand for the full national song.He accused Congress of politicising the issue. “They (Congress) should have stopped this (the law mandating full rendition of the national song) in Parliament. When Congress comes to power, and I pray the Congress comes to power as soon as possible, they can revoke this in Parliament. Let them do it, we have no objection,” Omar told reporters.Congress MP K C Venugopal triggered the war of words on Wednesday, by asking National Conference to “honour the wisdom and judgement of our freedom fighters” and stand with INDIA bloc in singing only the first two stanzas of the national song.
Article Summary: Omar Abdullah accused Congress of politicising the issue. “The entire stanza of national song Vande Mataram must be played across the country at the govt events,” the CM said, adding legal action could be taken against those who fail to stand for the full national song.

Article Title: Retro looks, current jibes: Netas give '80s a new spin
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: "The 80s called, I answered," quipped agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan as he posted on X a picture of him from that era. Congress Kerala posted an invented Gujarat street scene; BJP Telangana replied with a fabricated bar scene tagged "Lusiana, Italy", apparently alluding to Sonia Gandhi's birthplace.The '80s came calling, and India's politicians answered with aviators, old albums and a little swagger. Then party accounts joined the nostalgia trip, remembering to pack a few jibes for the other side.Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal shared an AI portrait of himself in a suit and aviators, saying: "Vibing to the 80s trend". Union ports, shipping and waterways minister Sarbananda Sonowal wrote: "80s vibes: Styles fade, but the appeal is forever!" A line fit for a campaign, vintage or otherwise.Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma chimed in: "Back to the 80s eh!" Telangana CM Revanth Reddy appeared beside a motorbike in his post. For a while, the competition seemed to be over who wore the decade best.Others let their albums do the talking. Congress neta Renuka Chowdhury offered a reality check: "Me? I've got receipts." She shared what she de-scribed as an '80s Savvy magazine cover featuring herself.Union minister Kiren Rijiju followed his AI makeover with a throwback he said needed neither AI nor ChatGPT.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor posted pictures with his sons, Ishaan and Kanishk. "I thought I'd join the trend the old-fashioned way," he wrote, a real photograph a boast of its own amid the trend built on imagining the past.BJP's Tamilisai Soundararajan shared wedding footage featuring then chief minister MGR and opposition leader M Karunanidhi. Rival camps on one guest list.The party accounts added their own gloss. BJP Tamil Nadu's montage of PM Narendra Modi mixed AI styling with archival photographs, ending with "karmayogi". Congress Sevadal posted AI images of Rahul Gandhi.Then came the knowing captions. Congress Kerala's AI image showed a bald man in an Omni van: "A Gujarat street in the 80s." A roadside sign said in Hindi: "Please smile, you are in Delhi." BJP Telangana's bar scene was dated "Circa-1970's". Neither named its target.The clothes belonged to another decade. The urge to have the last word was entirely up to date.
Article Summary: The '80s came calling, and India's politicians answered with aviators, old albums and a little swagger. Then party accounts joined the nostalgia trip, remembering to pack a few jibes for the other side. Congress Kerala posted an invented Gujarat street scene; BJP Telangana replied with a fabricated bar scene.

Article Title: IRCTC case: Laundering charges framed against Lalu Prasad Yadav, kin
Article Text: NEW DELHI/PATNA: A Delhi court Thursday framed charges against RJD chief Lalu Prasad , wife Rabri Devi, their son, Tejashwi Prasad Yadav, and six others in a money laundering case linked to the alleged IRCTC hotel scam, report Koushiki Saha & Jai Narain Pandey. The case dates to Lalu's tenure as railway minister in the UPA govt (2004-09).Special judge Vishal Gogne of Rouse Avenue Court observed that tenders for leasing two IRCTC hotels at Ranchi and Puri were manipulated by railway officials under the "stewardship" of Lalu as he framed the charges under PMLA. The others against whom charges were framed included M/s Lara Projects, former RJD Union minister Premchand Gupta and and his wife, Sarla.
Article Summary: A Delhi court Thursday framed charges against RJD chief Lalu Prasad. The case dates to Lalu's tenure as railway minister in the UPA govt (2004-09) The court observed that tenders for leasing two IRCTC hotels at Ranchi and Puri were manipulated by railway officials under the "stewardship" of Lalu.

Article Title: IRCTC scam case: Delhi court orders framing of charges against Lalu, Rabri Devi and Tejashwi
Article Text:
The court cited 'strong suspicion of abuse of office' against Lalu in IRCTC hotels case

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Thursday ordered the framing of charges against former railway minister Lalu Prasad Yadav and others in the alleged IRCTC hotels money laundering case, observing that there was a strong suspicion of abuse of office during his tenure.The court said railway officials manipulated the tender process under Prasad’s stewardship to facilitate the award of leases for IRCTC-run hotels in Ranchi and Pune. It also said the nature, timing and course of the investigation in the case were not inspired by political vendetta, reported PTI.The court also ordered framing of charges against former Bihar chief minister Rabri Devi, her son Tejashwi Yadav, Lara Projects, Sujata Hotels and four others. The charges include corruption, criminal conspiracy and cheating against Lalu Prasad, while Rabri Devi and Tejashwi face conspiracy and cheating charges.The case stems from alleged irregularities in the award of contracts to operate two IRCTC hotels. The CBI has alleged that the tender process was manipulated and conditions were tweaked to favour Sujata Hotels during Lalu Prasad's tenure as railway minister. The ED has alleged that the transactions were part of a larger money-laundering conspiracy.The accused have pleaded not guilty and the case will now proceed to trial. The framing of charges and the court's observations at this stage do not amount to a finding of guilt.
Article Summary: The court said railway officials manipulated the tender process under Prasad’s stewardship to facilitate the award of leases for IRCTC-run hotels in Ranchi and Pune. The court also ordered framing of charges against former Bihar chief minister Rabri Devi, her son Tejashwi Yadav, Lara Projects, Sujata Hotels and four others.

Article Title: FIR registered against Azam Khan, four others over Hajj land irregularities
Article Text:
FIR has been registered against five people, including Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan

NEW DELHI: An FIR has been registered against five people, including Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan , over alleged irregularities in the use of Hajj Committee land.The FIR has been registered under charges of fraud, criminal conspiracy and provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act.The Vigilance Department has named former Hajj Committee chairman Azam Khan and two former secretaries in its probe into the alleged irregularities.The proprietor of Amish Developers and two others have also been named as accused in the case.The allegations state that regulations were bypassed during the land sale to benefit a private firm.A Vigilance Department probe found that the alleged irregularities caused a revenue loss of Rs 2,08,95,000 to the Hajj Committee.Khan, a prominent Samajwadi Party leader from Rampur, was first jailed in February 2020 after surrendering in a forgery case. He was later shifted to Sitapur jail, while his wife and son, who were also booked in cases, were released earlier.According to police records, Khan has been named as an accused in 111 criminal cases, including those related to forgery and land encroachment. Final reports have been filed in seven cases, one case resulted in his discharge, and nine were withdrawn by the Samajwadi Party government. He was convicted in six cases but has since secured bail in all of them. The remaining cases are still under trial.One of the prominent cases against Khan is the Quality Bar land case, in which he was accused of misusing his position as cabinet minister in 2013 to facilitate the allotment of land to a family member.
Article Summary: FIR has been registered against five people, including Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan. Allegations state that regulations were bypassed during the land sale to benefit a private firm. Khan has been named as an accused in 111 criminal cases, including those related to forgery and land encroachment.

Article Title: Quack doctor detained in Maharashtra for practising medicine without registration
Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: FIR lodged after 3,400 SIR forms found in Navi Mumbai shop; 5 BLOs suspended
Article Text:
An FIR was registered against Suraj Patil for illegally possessing voter enumeration forms





NAVI MUMBAI: The police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting special intensive revision (SIR) voter enumeration forms for “personal use” and for breaking the maintenance of secrecy of voting under Section 314 of the BNS and Section 128 of the Representation of People Act.Section 314 of the BNS deals with dishonestly converting a movable property for own use, for which the punishment is at least two years imprisonment.The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar. He alerted the police.The accused (Patil) had decamped from the Kharghar police station, leading to high drama throughout the night.Authorities seized 3,404 SIR forms, including 11 blank ones, of 11 polling stations from the photocopier’s shop next to the Ramsheth Thakur Public School in Sector 19, Kharghar, by Shiv Sena (UBT) nodal chief Balesh Bhojane.Five booth-level officers (BLOs) served with show-cause notices were suspended by the Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) chief Mangesh Chitale.They include three data entry operators working as booth-level officers from a private company, Saunik Integrated & Security Pvt Ltd, Bhayandar, engaged by the PCMC.Their names are Sulochana Mane, Prashant Mhatre and Rahul Bhagat.The Shiv Sena (UBT) had earlier warned the Panvel sub-divisional officer through a letter about various lapses in the electoral process.A two-member inquiry committee comprising a Panvel deputy municipal commissioner, Nanasaheb Kamathe, and an assistant electoral registration officer, has been formed to conduct a comprehensive probe.Bhojane said, “MLAs Jitendra Awhad and Rohit Pawar have tweeted the video regarding the original SIR forms at the Kharghar shop. We demand action against the Panvel SDO as he did not take preventive measures despite our complaint about forms filed at the BJP offices. The FIR was filed only after more than hundreds of our workers assembled at the police station.”After learning about the incident, Raigad district communication head of Shiv Sena (UBT) Prasad Bhoir lodged a complaint with the electoral registration officer.“Yesterday evening, the election registration office (ERO) received information that a person is xeroxing enumeration forms at a Xerox centre at Kharghar sector 19. Immediately, the assistant election registration officer visited the site and found that one Suraj Patil was holding around 3,400 enumeration forms and xeroxing it illegally,” Raigad district collector Kishan Javale said.
Article Summary: Police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting voter enumeration forms. The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar.

Article Title: Shiv Sena leader Rahul Gharat arrested in Palghar hospital doctor assault case
Article Text:
A Shiv Sena leader was arrested after a hospital ruckus involving injured Govindas

MLA seeks action against doctors





PALGHAR: Shiv Sena (Shinde faction) Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, the main accused in the alleged ruckus and assault at a private hospital in Palghar, was arrested on Monday after he surrendered before the police.The incident took place at Relief Hospital in Palghar on Saturday night when five injured Govindas, who had sustained injuries during Dahi Handi celebrations, were admitted for treatment. Three of them were kept in the intensive care unit (ICU).The injured Govindas had alleged that the hospital was forcing them to undergo CT scans and was trying to charge them excessive amounts. Following the allegations, Shiv Sena office-bearers and workers entered the hospital late at night and allegedly created a ruckus. A hospital employee was assaulted and the IV lines of the Govindas admitted to the ICU were allegedly removed before they were taken away.Palghar police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, city chief Rahul Gharat, the son of MLA Rajendra Gavit and deputy taluka chief Rohit Gavit, under various sections of the law.“Gharat appeared before the Palghar police station on Monday and was arrested.Efforts are on to trace the remaining accused,” said Kishor Manbhav, senior police inspector of Palghar police station.Meanwhile, injured Govinda Akash Patil reiterated his allegations against the doctors. He claimed that although he felt better after being given an injection, he was allegedly kept in the ICU for three hours after being put on a saline drip against his wishes. He demanded action against the doctors.Palghar MLA Rajendra Gavit visited the Palghar police station on Monday and demanded that a case be registered against the doctors.Gavit alleged that the hospital staff were forcing the injured Govindas to stay back and undergo MRI and CT scans. He said Shiv Sena workers had gone to the hospital to help the injured Govindas and that a verbal altercation had taken place.He alleged that the doctors had filed a complaint against the Shiv Sena workers out of vendetta and pressured the police to register a case. “Can a patient not even question a doctor about an excessive bill?” Gavit asked, demanding that the police register a case against the doctors.
Article Summary: Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, the main accused in the alleged ruckus and assault at a private hospital in Palghar, was arrested on Monday. The incident took place at Relief Hospital on Saturday night when five injured Govindas, who had sustained injuries during Dahi Handi celebrations, were admitted for treatment. Three of them were kept in the intensive care unit.

Article Title: Six armed men rob farmer’s house in Daund village
Article Text:
Photo for representation

Pune:





A gang of six armed men barged into a farmer’s house at Malthan village in Daund taluka, about 108km from Pune, and robbed a gold chain and two cellphones collectively worth Rs86,000.The farmer’s son, who resisted the accused, sustained severe head injuries after being assaulted with a sharp weapon. The dacoity took place in the early hours of Wednesday. Farmer Bhagwan Dalvi (51) lodged a complaint with the Daund police.An officer from the Pune Rural police said that around 2.30am on Wednesday, the six armed men barged into the complainant’s house. When the complainant’s son, Swapnil Dalvi, started resisting them, the accused assaulted him with sharp weapons. “They snatched a gold chain from a woman in the house. They also snatched two mobile handsets and fled on two motorcycles,” the officer said.He said the farmer then alerted his neighbours and the police. “We have registered a case under sections 310 (dacoity) and 311 (robbery or dacoity with an attempt to cause death or grievous hurt) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS),” he said.

Article Title: Cops arrest SUV owner from Tathawade for using auto-hiding number plate, released on bail
Article Text:
The SUV was spotted on a highway recently

Pune:





Wakad police on Thursday arrested an SUV owner from Tathawade for using an auto-hiding number plate to avoid traffic challans. The SUV owner, Vijay Dagade (44), was produced before a court and released on bail.“During the investigation, Dagade told us that he brought the auto-hiding number plate from Punjab ,” an officer from Wakad police said. Dagade was tracked down by the Pimpri Chinchwad RTO after a video of his SUV’s auto-hiding number plate, purportedly shot on the Pune-Mumbai Expressway, circulated on social media. The RTO penalised him Rs4,500 for an unauthorised alteration to his vehicle. The RTO also found that the vehicle had 55 pending challans, amounting to Rs1.22 lakh. Most of the challans were issued for over speeding.Wakad police on Wednesday suo motu registered a case against Dagade. He has been charged under sections 336 (forgery), 318 (cheating) and 319 (cheating by personation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Dagade’s lawyer, Vijaysinh Thombare, told the court that though the alleged offence was serious, it was his first offence and he had no criminal record. Judicial Magistrate First Class Dipti Patil granted bail to Dagade on a personal bond of Rs25,000 and surety of the same amount. The court also warned him against committing any offence in the future.
Article Summary: SUV owner Vijay Dagade (44) was produced before a court and released on bail. Dagade was tracked down by the Pimpri Chinchwad RTO after a video of his SUV’s auto-hiding number plate, purportedly shot on the Pune-Mumbai Expressway, circulated on social media.

Article Title: 10 lakh voters dropped in Nashik, zero objections filed so far
Article Text:
Divisional commissioner Pravin Gedam held meeting of the election officials in Nashik today

Nashik





: The district election office has deleted 10.3 lakh electors’ names across all 15 assembly constituencies under the special intensive electoral roll revision 2026.The administration has received zero claims or objections from those affected so far. In light of this, divisional commissioner and electoral roll observer Pravin Gedam has urged political parties to appoint booth level agents (BLAs) to ensure no eligible voter is left out of the process.Gedam reviewed the situation during a visit to the district collectorate on Thursday, holding meetings with election officials, legislators, and political party representatives. The draft electoral roll was published on Aug 31. The secondary phase, running from Aug 31 to Sept 30, allows citizens to submit claims and objections. Following this window, Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) will conduct hearings through Oct 29 to execute final inclusions and corrections.Deputy district election officer Madhumati Sardesai noted the stark concentration of the purge. “We have received no claims or objections yet. The maximum number of deletions is from four urban assembly segments—Nashik Central, Nashik West, Nashik East, and Deolali. Collectively, the names of 5.5 lakh electors have been deleted from just these four constituencies. ”During the meeting, which was attended by legislators Nitin Arjun Pawar, Hiraman Khoskar, and Seema Hiray, political representatives flagged concerns that booth level officers (BLOs) were failing to conduct door-to-door visits in urban areas.Responding to the feedback, Gedam stated, “The implementation of the Special Intensive Electoral Roll Revision program must be scrutinized thoroughly. Registration officers must exercise strict vigilance to ensure field officers complete their visits and gather forms appropriately. ”Gedam appealed to eligible electors and citizens categorized under ‘absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate’ (ASD) to submit their claims to registration officers by September 30. Youths turning 18 on or before Oct 1 are urged to enrol using Form 6. To facilitate this, special camps will be organised at polling centers on Sept 19, 20, 26, and 27, where BLOs will be present from 10 AM to 6 PM.
Article Summary: The district election office has deleted 10.3 lakh electors’ names across all 15 assembly constituencies under the special intensive electoral roll revision 2026. The administration has received zero claims or objections from those affected so far. Divisional commissioner and electoral roll observer Pravin Gedam has urged political parties to appoint booth level agents to ensure no eligible voter is left out of the process.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan first to file nomination
Article Text:
K Padmarajan filling his nomination





TIRUPUR: Filing of nominations for the Dharapuram reserved (scheduled caste) assembly bypoll in Tirupur district began at 11am on Wednesday, with self-styled “Election King” K Padmarajan becoming the first candidate to submit papers before revenue divisional officer A Felix Raja. He is contesting as an independent candidatePadmarajan, a tyre shop owner from Attur in Salem district, said this was his 256th nomination since 1988, filed in Tamil Nadu and other states to underline that ordinary citizens could also contest elections. He claimed that the effort was also part of a Guinness record attempt, adding that he had previously contested against leaders including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, former chief ministers J Jayalalithaa, M Karunanidhi and MK Stalin, and chief minister C Joseph Vijay. He had spent lakhs of rupees on filing nominations over the years.According to the election schedule, nominations can be filed till Sept 16. Scrutiny will be held on Sept 17, and the last date for withdrawal is Sept 19. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.The Dharapuram constituency has been a reserved seat since 1967. The constituency has seen shifting electoral outcomes in recent cycles, with AIADMK winning in 2011, Congress in 2016 and DMK in 2021, before the seat returned to AIADMK in the last assembly election.It is for the first time that a bypoll is going to be held in Tirupur district, which was formed in 2009. The bypoll has been necessitated by the resignation of R Sathyabama, who was the sitting MLA. Sathyabhama, who contested on behalf of AIADMK, won the election from Dharapuram constituency by securing 81,100 votes. She voted in support of the TVK during the floor test in the assembly and subsequently resigned from her MLA post and joined the TVK.Meanwhile, DMK on Wednesday announced S Suganya,33, a lawyer and party women’s wing functionary, as its candidate in the constituency.
Article Summary: Self-styled ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan became the first candidate to submit papers. He said this was his 256th nomination since 1988. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.

Article Title: Cleric held under Pocso Act for harassing eight-year-old girl
Article Text:
A 27-year-old cleric attached to a madrasah in Sivaganga district was arrested under the Pocso Act for allegedly sexually harassing an eight-year-old girl.

Sivaganga:





A 27-year-old cleric attached to a madrasah in Sivaganga district was arrested under the Pocso Act for allegedly sexually harassing an eight-year-old girl.Police said the Class II student had been attending the madrasah attached to a mosque for the past two years. The accused, Ansari of Thondi in Ramanathapuram district, had been working as a religious instructor at the madrasah for the past four years.According to police, the girl told her mother that the cleric had subjected her to sexual harassment. The mother lodged a complaint with Sakottai police, based on which police registered a case under relevant sections of the Pocso Act and arrested Ansari.After interrogation, Ansari was remanded in judicial custody on Wednesday. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A 27-year-old cleric attached to a madrasah in Sivaganga district was arrested under the Pocso Act. The girl told her mother that the cleric had subjected her to sexual harassment. The Class II student had been attending the madrasa for the past two years.

Article Title: Bangladesh national escapes from police custody
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Palarivattom police on Thursday intensified the search for a 31-year-old Bangladesh national who escaped from police custody at Palarivattom police station on Wednesday night. He and five other undocumented Bangladesh nationals were arrested by the police on Wednesday.The accused, identified as Hadiullah Khan, 31, a native of Morrelganj in Bagerhat district of Bangladesh, escaped from police custody around 8.30pm. According to the FIR in the escape case, Hadiullah was in lawful custody at the station at 8.30pm on Wednesday when police were recording his fingerprints. He allegedly entered the bathroom in a room on the first floor of the station and escaped by jumping through a window.He was the sixth accused in the case registered under sections 21 and 23(a) of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. According to the police, a police party were on patrol around 3.30am on Wednesday when they received credible confidential information that several Bangladeshi nationals were staying illegally on Savitha Road in the Vennala area.The police team reached the location and conducted a verification at the building around 3.40am.The occupants were identified as Ibrahim Howlader, 39; Sakeer Khan, 50; Arif Howlader, 29; Unus Khan, 41; Joshana Begum, 30; and Hadiullah Khan. All six were from Morrelganj in Bagerhat district of Bangladesh, said the police.Police said the six had entered India illegally and were staying in the rented building without passports, visas or other supporting documents. Joshana Begum and Unus Khan were also allegedly staying there with their children, aged nine and two-and-a-half years.The six adults were informed about the alleged offence and arrested at the spot. Mobile phones found in their possession were seized and taken into custody after being recorded in the seizure mahazar. The accused were subsequently taken to the Palarivattom police station. Hadiullah Khan managed to escape when the police were busy processing the arrested persons
Article Summary: The accused, identified as Hadiullah Khan, 31, a native of Morrelganj in Bagerhat district of Bangladesh, escaped from police custody around 8.30pm. He allegedly entered the bathroom in a room on the first floor of the station and escaped by jumping through a window. He was the sixth accused in the case registered under sections 21 and 23(a) of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.
